name: Ludwig von Mises
period: Classical-liberal writings, 1927–1962; policies assessed from his theoretical programme
description: Austrian economist assessed through his writings on private ownership, market coordination, limited government, migration and peaceful political change.

religion.reason: The biographical account explicitly describes adult Mises as agnostic; Jewish ancestry does not establish a religious prerequisite.

sources.title: Ludwig von Mises — biography and positions

axes.brief: Democratic replacement prevents civil war; representative institutions and minority rights bound majority decisions.
axes.counterEvidence: His qualified 1927 praise of fascism as an emergency measure contradicts a spotless democratic record.

axes.brief: Limited coercion should protect persons and property rather than impose morality or paternalistic choices.
axes.counterEvidence: He retained police against aggression; public infection and preventive restrictions differ from self-regarding choices.

axes.brief: Voluntary cultural affiliation and tolerance oppose coercive assimilation and state cultural patronage.
axes.counterEvidence: Publicly funded accommodation is also state expenditure; tolerance does not mean distinct customs always take precedence.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: Freedom of migration follows free movement of labour and opposition to coercive national privileges.
axes.counterEvidence: Welfare entitlement and undocumented admission are different mechanisms; language conflict in interventionist states remains relevant.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: Peaceful exchange and opposition to imperial conquest favour diplomacy and arms reduction.
axes.counterEvidence: Defence against aggression remains legitimate; avoiding war at all costs is stronger than his liberal peace programme.

axes.brief: International cooperation and open exchange aim to reduce conflict without abolishing consensual self-determination.
axes.counterEvidence: A supranational government can become coercive; monetary competition differs from compulsory currency pooling.

axes.brief: Private productive ownership and calculation through competitive markets are fundamental to his programme.
axes.counterEvidence: Government remains for security and justice; this is not an argument for anarchy.

axes.brief: He rejects protectionist privileges and restrictions on international exchange and investment.
axes.counterEvidence: Security of persons and contracts is retained; these statements specify economic barriers rather than criminal fraud.

axes.brief: Market prices, private investment and calculation oppose production commands, subsidies and imposed wage schedules.
axes.counterEvidence: Privately issued currency is qualified by his monetary proposals; strong market advocacy is not an observed policy implementation.

axes.brief: Redistributive taxation and intervention distort private property and market incentives in his analysis.
axes.counterEvidence: Private charity is legitimate; opposition to compulsory benefits does not imply opposition to helping poor people.

axes.brief: Secular utilitarian law and tolerance support separation of religious authority from government.
axes.counterEvidence: Voluntary faith remains respected; existing public holidays are less intrusive than church-directed law.

axes.brief: Personal freedom permits voluntary departures from inherited customs without compulsory social transformation.
axes.counterEvidence: His writings retain conventional family assumptions; legal liberty does not prove modern identity-language preferences.

axes.brief: Entrepreneurship and technological development favour experimentation rather than broad prior prohibition.
axes.counterEvidence: Liability for harm and uncertain irreversible effects qualify permission; no modern biomedical stance is documented.

axes.brief: Local self-determination, secession and decentralisation reduce coercion between national groups.
axes.counterEvidence: A limited central state may coordinate immediate defence or disasters; decentralisation is not compulsory local collectivism.

axes.brief: Human cooperation and common rational action reject race-specific logic while recognising differences among individuals.
axes.counterEvidence: Praxeology does not specify genetic causal shares for temperament, attention or sex differences.
